title: Minimum Number of Flips to Make the Binary String Alternating
summary: Given a binary string, determine the least number of type-2 operations needed to make the string alternating.
statement: Given a binary string, determine the least number of type-2 operations needed to make the string alternating. Type-2 operations involve flipping any character from '0' to '1' or vice versa. Type-1 operations allow moving the first character to the end. An alternating string has no two consecutive identical characters.
constraints: Moving the first character to the end costs nothing and may be repeated.
A paid operation flips one chosen bit; minimize paid flips needed for an alternating result.
hints: Every rotation is a length-n window in the doubled string s+s.
Track mismatches against the global 0101... pattern while adding the right character and removing the expired left character.
For each full window, its mismatches against 1010... are n minus the tracked count.
The doubled windows enumerate every rotation exactly once, and the two complementary counts cover both alternating targets.
editorial: The doubled windows enumerate every rotation exactly once, and the two complementary counts cover both alternating targets.

tests.explanation: A free rotation followed by two flips is optimal.
The input is already alternating, so zero flips are needed.
